faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award/agreement-free employees.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for quick calculations.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, casual employees earn $33.05 per hour. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate: From Minimum Wage to Award Rates

Whether you're earning the National Minimum Wage or a figure closer to Sam Worthington's Avatar salary, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and understanding your entitlements. This guide explains the process using official Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission data, and highlights the differences between minimum rates, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation.

### The National Minimum Wage (2026–27)

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, equating to $1004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum $33.05 per hour. These rates apply to award/agreement-free employees and are set by the Fair Work Commission. For most workers, award rates are higher—check the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your industry.

### Award Rates vs. the Minimum Wage

Awards set minimum pay rates for specific industries and occupations. For example, the Health Services Award saw changes from 1 October 2026, and the SCHADS Award (Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services) will receive increases from 1 December 2026. Always refer to the relevant pay guide rather than assuming the National Minimum Wage applies. Our [reference tables](/data) list common award classifications.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of their base rate. This is not a separate rate—it's an addition. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, enter your base hourly rate and tick the casual loading box; never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost for employers. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Converting Hourly to Annual Salary: The Formula

The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week. For example:
- $26.44/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,253 per year (National Minimum Wage)
- $33.05/hour (casual) × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $65,317 per year

To find your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly earnings by 2. For the minimum wage, that's $2009.80 per fortnight before tax.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Sam Worthington's Avatar Salary in Context

Sam Worthington's salary for the Avatar films has not been publicly disclosed, but reports suggest it is in the millions—far above any award rate. Even so, the same conversion principle applies: his hourly rate (assuming a standard work year) would be his annual salary divided by 52 weeks and then by hours worked per week. While his earnings are exceptional, the formula remains universal. For most Australians, the National Minimum Wage or an award rate is the starting point.

### Using Our Tools

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate, add casual loading, and instantly see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. For award-specific rates, visit the [pay guides](/blog) page. Remember that these estimates assume consistent hours, no unpaid overtime, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% on top, and tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Key Takeaways

- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour ($33.05 casual) for 38 hours.
- Award rates often exceed the minimum—check your industry's pay guide.
- Annual salary = hourly × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time).
- Fortnightly pay = weekly × 2.
- Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings, up to the contribution cap.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay—use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

Whether you're earning the minimum or a figure like Sam Worthington's Avatar salary, understanding these conversions helps you make informed financial decisions.
